status: Failed attempted product obstruction; unreviewed working countercheck
own_argument:
UNREVIEWED working countercheck, not a theorem grant or classification. Let each tripod be the three rays generated by e1,e2,-e1-e2 with unit balancing weights and primitive radial coordinate t>=0. Its only positive zero relation has equal coefficients. For epsilon>0 rational and a chosen ray A, define h_A=t+3(epsilon-t)_+ on A and h_A=t+3epsilon on either other ray. It is continuous, integral-slope/rational-constant PA: outgoing slopes at the origin are-2,1,1, whose sum is0, and the sole interior break on A increases slope by3. Hence direct one-dimensional PCC/Jensen inequalities hold. The same construction h_B holds on the second tripod. Their sum phi=h_A+h_B on the product is PC: project every permitted product PCC to each factor, apply its Jensen inequality and add. Endpoint rationality/common-face incidence is preserved by both linear projections. Its difference from gamma=t1+t2 is bounded.

Define u_cross=max(epsilon-min(t1,t2),0) on the chosen quadrant A times B and u_cross=epsilon on every other quadrant. The definitions agree on all shared axes, so u_cross is bounded continuous literal PA. Suppose one tries to transfer the U(3,4) formula to this product by declaring P_try=gamma+3u_cross. This fails for obstacle gamma+C u_cross whenever C>=6. On the selected quadrant, each of (epsilon-t1)_+ and (epsilon-t2)_+ is at most u_cross, so phi-gamma=3[(epsilon-t1)_++(epsilon-t2)_+]<=6u_cross<=C u_cross. Outside that quadrant each correction is at most3epsilon, so again phi-gamma<=6epsilon<=Cepsilon. Thus phi is an actual admissible PC competitor below the obstacle, but phi(0)=6epsilon while P_try(0)=3epsilon. Therefore P_try cannot be the envelope.

This is only a failed attempted obstruction with a separating competitor. No exact product envelope, MA assignment, contact identity, real regularization theorem or arbitrary nonseparable-obstacle classification has been proved. It does not alter the accepted strict-growth U(3,4) result, which has a different fan. The native190 original classification input remains unchanged; no hot feedback was sent.
